title: Blackjack hand value
starter:
type suit = Hearts | Diamonds | Clubs | Spades
type card =
  | Number of int * suit        (* 2 through 10 *)
  | Jack of suit | Queen of suit | King of suit
  | Ace of suit

(* Number n is worth n, faces 10, an Ace 11; but each Ace may drop to 1 while the total is over 21. *)
let hand_value (hand : card list) : int =
  0
hints: Score the hand as if every Ace is 11 first, then fix it up.
Write a `points` function with one pattern per card shape, sum the hand with `List.fold_left`, and count the Aces.
While the total is over 21 and you still have an Ace counted as 11, subtract 10. A small recursive helper that takes the total and the Aces left does it.

answer.code:
type suit = Hearts | Diamonds | Clubs | Spades
type card =
  | Number of int * suit        (* 2 through 10 *)
  | Jack of suit | Queen of suit | King of suit
  | Ace of suit

let hand_value (hand : card list) : int =
  let points = function Number (n, _) -> n | Jack _ | Queen _ | King _ -> 10 | Ace _ -> 11 in
  let total = List.fold_left (fun acc c -> acc + points c) 0 hand in
  let aces = List.length (List.filter (function Ace _ -> true | _ -> false) hand) in
  let rec soften t a = if t > 21 && a > 0 then soften (t - 10) (a - 1) else t in
  soften total aces
answer.explain: The reference scores each card with a pattern match (Aces as 11), sums with `List.fold_left`, then softens: while the total is over 21 and some Ace is still worth 11, it subtracts 10. Two Aces become 12, not 22 or 2.
